# Feature-Store Specification for Empirically Grounding the Direction of Product A/B Experiments

**Purpose.** This schema exists to let an empirical/causal engine predict the *outcome DIRECTION (sign)* of a roadmap A/B test by (a) expressing the treatment as a shift in a feature the store already shows to be predictive of the target metric, (b) reading the exposed population's standing propensity and historical elasticity to that lever, and (c) carrying the moderators that flip the sign. It is organized around **mechanism estimands and OEC metric families**, not around UI surfaces. The honest design goal is a *router* — answer where the lever is feature-expressible and historically varied; **abstain** where it is aesthetic, cold-start, interference-dominated, or driven by long-horizon/novelty dynamics. Anchored in real practice: DoorDash (~12k experiments/yr, 3-sided OEC, CUPED/CUPAC, switchback), Booking.com (1000s of concurrent UI/copy tests), Airbnb (Minerva ~12k metrics / 4k dimensions, cluster-randomization), Tecton/Feast entity model (user/merchant/item/session/market as join-keyed entities with windowed aggregates).

---

## 1. Experiment-Type Taxonomy

Weighted by realistic share of a consumer-marketplace roadmap. Grouped by family.

### 1.1 UI / interaction / flow (the bulk of volume — ~40–55%)

| Type | Freq | Example |
|---|---|---|
| CTA / button copy, affordance & placement | very-common | "Order now" → "Get it in 25 min"; move CTA above the fold; enlarge tap target |
| Layout / module reorder & information hierarchy | very-common | Promote "reorder your last order" carousel above promo banners |
| Copy / messaging / microcopy | very-common | Headline, value-prop wording, button label, tone |
| Form / checkout flow: field & step count | very-common | Collapse 3-step checkout to one scroll page; remove a form field |
| Checkout / cart friction reduction | very-common | One-tap reorder + saved-card default; guest checkout |
| Onboarding / first-run / signup funnel | common | Defer location-permission ask to first search; collapse 4 steps to 2 |
| Navigation / IA restructure | common | Split "Account" into "Orders" + "Profile"; rename "Pickup" → "Skip the line" |
| Default selection / pre-fill / opt-in vs opt-out | common | Pre-select 18% tip; default "Standard" delivery; auto-enroll notifications |
| Latency / performance optimization | common | Prefetch store page on hover (1.2s → 0.6s); skeleton screens |
| Content density / truncation ("show more") | common | 4 vs 8 menu items before "see all"; clamp descriptions to 2 lines |
| Search & filter / discovery UI | common | Inline filter chips vs modal sheet; add "under 30 min" one-tap chip |
| Modal / interstitial / popup timing & dismissibility | common | Subscription upsell after first add-to-cart vs at app open |
| Friction add/remove guardrail (confirm steps, one-click) | occasional | One-click reorder with no review screen; add "is this address right?" |
| Media / thumbnail / autoplay | occasional | Add dish photos to menu rows; autoplay store-card preview |
| Empty / error / loading-state design | occasional | Spinner → skeleton list; add "browse nearby" CTA to no-results |

### 1.2 Pricing / promo / monetization (~15–20%)

| Type | Freq | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Fee / price-level change | common | Drop delivery fee $3.99 → $1.99 on orders < $15; measure conversion + net revenue |
| Promo / discount / threshold incentive | very-common | "$0 delivery over $25"; "$5 off first order" vs free delivery |
| Price framing / display (anchor, bundling, itemization, drip vs all-in) | common | All-in price upfront vs fees-at-checkout |
| Subscription / paywall / membership pricing | common | $9.99 vs $7.99/mo; 30- vs 14-day trial; upsell after 3rd order |
| Dynamic / surge / personalized pricing | occasional | New surge curve throttling demand on short supply (needs switchback) |
| Default tip / pre-checked add-on monetization | common | Default tip 15% vs 18% vs none |
| Upsell / cross-sell / basket building | common | "Add a drink" module at cart; frequently-bought-together |
| Loyalty / rewards / gamification | occasional | 10th order free vs 5% cashback; order-streak progress bar |
| Referral / invite incentive | occasional | Symmetric $10/$10 vs $15/$5 give-get |
| Wallet / stored-value / gift-card / BNPL / payment-method *(critic add)* | occasional | Default stored-value instrument; offer BNPL at checkout |

### 1.3 Ranking / recommendation / relevance (~10–15%)

| Type | Freq | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Search ranking / sort / result-ordering | very-common | Default sort "most popular" → "fastest delivery"; pCVR-weighted ranker |
| Recommendation / personalization module | very-common | Replace popularity recs with collaborative-filtering on home feed |
| Algorithmic / ML model swap (ETA, ranker, pricing model) | occasional | Heuristic ETA → gradient-boosted ETA |
| Trust / social-proof / scarcity elements | common | "ordered 200+ times this week"; "only 3 left"; verified badge |

### 1.4 Lifecycle / messaging (~5–10%)

| Type | Freq | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Push/email/in-app notification (content, timing, frequency, channel) | very-common | "your usual is back" push before habitual order time; +2nd daily push |
| Badge / re-engagement / win-back prompt | common | Cart-abandon nudge copy; badge dot vs numeric count |

### 1.5 Marketplace / supply-side / equilibrium (~5–10%)

| Type | Freq | Example |
|---|---|---|
| ETA / availability / inventory display | occasional | Conservative vs tight ETA; "busy" status |
| Supply-side / merchant or host tooling | occasional | Prompt merchants to add item photos; smart-pricing suggestions |
| Two-sided supply incentive (courier pay, merchant commission/take-rate) | occasional | Peak-pay boost in undersupplied zones |
| Dispatch / matching / batching algorithm | rare | Batch two orders to one Dasher |
| Merchant/seller-as-product-user funnel & dashboard UX *(critic add)* | occasional | Host-onboarding funnel; ads-manager UX; self-serve menu editor |
| Structural pricing / business-model overhaul | rare | Per-order fees → all-in membership model |

### 1.6 Roadmap slices the council under-covered *(critic adds — flag as mostly abstain)*

| Type | Freq | Example | Coverage note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Acquisition / top-of-funnel / marketing-creative (paid ad, SEO/landing, app-store listing, logged-out web) | very-common (~10–20% of org roadmap) | Landing-page hero A/B; ad-creative test | **Un-keyable** — no anonymous visitor entity |
| Customer support / service / self-serve (chatbot vs human, deflection, refund automation) | common | Help-center deflection flow; refund auto-approve | OEC = contact-rate/CSAT/deflection; partially groundable via friction |
| Returns / refunds / cancellation-policy & post-purchase | common | Return-window length; order-tracking UX | **Where proximal→distal sign inverts** |
| Privacy / consent / compliance & account-management | common | Consent-prompt design; ATT; data-deletion flow | Mostly abstain; regulatory-threshold-driven |
| Internationalization / localization / accessibility | occasional | RTL layout; a11y modality; currency format | Groundable via friction for affected segments |
| Content moderation / integrity / fraud-decline friction | occasional | Demotion threshold; fraud-decline step | OEC = fraud loss vs good-user friction |
| Net-new feature / surface with no behavioral analog | occasional | Launch group-ordering or live-chat-with-store | **Hard floor — abstain** |
| Trust & safety / verification friction | rare | Require phone verification at signup | Trades friction for integrity |
| Brand / visual-identity / rename | rare | New palette + wordmark | **Near-unpredictable** |
| Pure visual / aesthetic redesign (color, hero image) | very-common | Green vs blue CTA | **Abstain — taste/novelty** |

## 2. The Exhaustive Feature-Store Schema (by Feature Class)

The council's ~67 proposed classes de-duplicate to **24 distinct classes** (~60% redundancy removed). Entities/join-keys: `user_id`, `visitor_id` (anonymous), `merchant_id`, `item_id`, `session_id`, `surface_id`/`variant_id`, `market_zone × time_bucket`, `experiment_id × arm × segment`.

> Notation per class: **Purpose · Columns · Source · Grain · Unlocks**. Source ∈ {transactions, telemetry, profile, experiment-history, external, derived}.

### A. Empirical anchor classes

**A1 — Experiment-history prior store (multi-grain)** *(merges marketplace surface×family, PM segment×family, pricing user×family, HCI experiment×arm×segment — the council's single largest redundancy)*
- **Purpose.** The meta-prior and the only asset that makes the engine *empirical* rather than a metrics dashboard: retrieve measured direction/magnitude of past experiments on the closest surface/family/segment/lever, by analogy/reference-class forecasting. Should dominate the prior where populated.
- **Columns.** `surface_id`, `treatment_family` (cta|layout|copy|flow|ranking|pricing|promo|notification|default|latency|…), `experiment_change_type`, `measured_friction_delta`, `historical_lift_sign_on_metric`, `historical_effect_size_p50`, `measured_effect_magnitude`, `n_prior_experiments`, `win_rate_for_family_on_surface`, `proximal_vs_distal_sign_agreement_flag`, `segment_heterogeneity_direction`, `segment_sign_flip_flag`, `novelty_decay_observed_flag`, `sample_size`, `power`, `neg_control_passed_flag`, `prior_<lever>_arm_response`, `historical_HTE_decile_<family>` (model-imputed, not measured — see §4).
- **Source.** experiment-history. **Grain.** multi: `(surface × treatment_family × metric)`, `(segment × experiment_family)`, `(user × experiment_family)`, `(experiment × arm × segment)`.
- **Unlocks.** Nearly all UI/copy/flow/ranking/pricing/promo/notification/default types.

**A2 — Pre-period covariates for variance reduction (CUPED/CUPAC)**
- **Purpose.** Not a direction signal but the causal glue: pre-treatment baselines + ML-predicted-baseline outcomes that de-noise estimates so weak directional signals separate (DoorDash Dash-AB). The same covariates that reduce variance also predict the outcome metric.
- **Columns.** `pre_period_primary_metric`, `predicted_outcome_baseline_cupac`, `pre_period_orders`, `pre_period_conversion_rate`, `cuped_covariate_outcome`.
- **Source.** derived. **Grain.** user. **Unlocks.** all powered-detection types (CTA, ranking, promo, model swap).

### B. User state / propensity classes

**B1 — Lifecycle + RFM + habit state** *(merges all four lenses' RFM/engagement/tenure/proficiency)*
- **Purpose.** Baseline propensity, headroom, saturation, inframarginality, and break-even crossing; the single most reused moderator. New vs core vs dormant users react oppositely to friction, paywalls, incentives. Also the CUPED pre-period value.
- **Columns.** `days_since_signup`, `account_age_days`, `lifecycle_stage` (new|activated|core|dormant|churned), `orders_lifetime`, `orders_l28d`, `orders_l30d`, `sessions_l7d`, `recency_days`, `days_since_last_order`, `frequency_decile`, `monetary_l90d`, `reorder_rate`, `reorder_share`, `order_cadence_regularity`, `habit_index_interpurchase_regularity`, `weekly_active_streak`, `is_activated_flag`, `lifetime_session_count`, `feature_adoption_breadth`, `power_user_decile`, `surface_visit_count_90d` (habituation/muscle-memory).
- **Source.** transactions + derived. **Grain.** user (+ user×surface for habituation). **Unlocks.** onboarding, lifecycle/notification, default, paywall, promo, loyalty, friction, nav/layout (habituation cost).

**B2 — Monetization state: value, churn-risk, subscription/membership** *(merges marketplace value/churn, PM loyalty/subscription, pricing subscription + lifecycle/churn)*
- **Purpose.** LTV, churn risk, and membership flip the marginal price a user faces (member = $0 delivery) and the sign of aggressive monetization; flags negative-ROI/inframarginal segments (subsidizing already-loyal users is pure cost).
- **Columns.** `ltv_pred`, `ltv_decile`, `churn_risk_score`, `subscription_propensity`, `incentive_roi_est`, `margin_per_user_l90d`, `is_subsidized_acquisition`, `is_member_flag`, `loyalty_tier`, `points_balance`, `subscription_tenure_days`, `renewal_propensity`, `renewal_proximity_days`, `trial_status`, `free_delivery_eligible_flag`, `member_break_even_orders`, `member_order_uplift`, `reactivation_count`.
- **Source.** profile + derived. **Grain.** user. **Unlocks.** paywall/subscription, fee/price, surge, promo, loyalty, lifecycle.

**B3 — Price/fee elasticity & deal-proneness** *(merges pricing's own-price-elasticity + deal-proneness + WTP, marketplace elasticity, PM elasticity)*
- **Purpose.** The most load-bearing quantity for any fee/price/promo/surge/threshold experiment: own-fee elasticity, promo-responsiveness (incremental vs give-away), and latent WTP/spend capacity. **Identifiability caveat in §4** — requires historical variation in the price actually shown.
- **Columns.** `fee_paid_p25_p50_p75_trailing_90d`, `orders_at_fee_above_median_rate`, `abandon_rate_when_fee_gt_3usd`, `checkout_abandon_vs_fee_slope`, `implied_fee_elasticity_segment`, `min_order_value_observed`, `pct_orders_with_coupon_180d`, `redemption_rate_offered_promos`, `avg_discount_depth_redeemed`, `orders_only_during_discount_flag`, `threshold_promo_basket_uplift`, `coupon_search_events_30d`, `estimated_price_elasticity`, `avg_basket_value_90d`, `tip_amount_median`, `premium_item_share`, `zip_median_income_external`, `spend_volatility`, `max_single_order_value`, `subsidy_dependence_flag`.
- **Source.** derived (from order/promo/impression logs). **Grain.** user (× fee-band). **Unlocks.** fee/price, promo/discount/threshold, paywall, surge, upsell, default.

**B4 — Reference-price & anchoring state** *(pricing-specific; signs framing tests)*
- **Purpose.** Carry the reference point a user codes a new price against (last-paid, recently-seen, category-typical) so a change is signed as a perceived gain/loss rather than an absolute dollar amount.
- **Columns.** `last_paid_price_same_item`, `avg_seen_price_category_30d`, `max_price_seen_session`, `discount_depth_vs_reference`, `anchor_seen_strikethrough_flag`, `price_gap_current_vs_reference_pct`, `days_since_last_purchase_category`.
- **Source.** derived (transactions + impressions). **Grain.** user × item-category. **Unlocks.** price framing/display, promo/discount, fee/price, scarcity.

**B5 — Preference / affinity / substitution & choice-set** *(merges marketplace affinity-embeddings, PM catalog-affinity, pricing substitution/choice-set)*
- **Purpose.** Encode taste, loyalty, novelty-seeking AND available alternatives/switching, so a ranking/rec/cross-sell change can be signed by match-quality and by whether it reallocates within-platform (zero-sum) or grows/loses total demand. Cross-elasticity is the ranking/surge sign driver.
- **Columns.** `category_affinity_vector`, `cuisine_top3`, `brand_loyalty_score`, `price_tier_pref`, `novelty_seeking_score`, `embedding_user_128d`, `repeat_merchant_share`, `single_merchant_loyalty_flag`, `n_merchants_in_radius`, `merchant_switch_rate_90d`, `category_concentration_hhi`, `avg_alternatives_per_search`, `cross_item_substitution_pairs`, `outside_option_strength_score`.
- **Source.** derived. **Grain.** user (× session × market for choice-set). **Unlocks.** recommendation/personalization, ranking/sort, cross-sell/upsell, search/discovery, model swap, surge/fee.

**B6 — Channel / notification responsiveness & fatigue** *(merges marketplace, PM, pricing — near-identical)*
- **Purpose.** Sign every messaging/cadence test: open/click/return per channel plus a saturation counter predict whether a marginal send lifts the under-messaged or pushes the fatigued to unsub/churn.
- **Columns.** `push_open_rate_l30d`, `email_ctr_l30d`, `push_opt_in_flag`, `msgs_received_l7d` (saturation), `sends_7d_fatigue_count`, `unsubscribe_propensity`, `unsubscribe_proximity_score`, `best_send_hour`, `channel_pref_vector`, `diminishing_return_slope_msg_count`.
- **Source.** telemetry/derived. **Grain.** user × channel. **Unlocks.** notification cadence, promo, referral, re-engagement, onboarding.

**B7 — Friction / cognitive-load & default-acceptance sensitivity** *(merges PM friction/cognitive-load + pricing default-acceptance/tip)*
- **Purpose.** Per-user tolerance for steps/choice and stickiness to presented defaults; decides whether adding a confirm or removing a field helps, and predicts default/tip-suggestion acceptance and its revenue effect. Choice-overload users react oppositely to power users.
- **Columns.** `form_abandon_propensity`, `decision_paralysis_score_choices_before_select`, `steps_tolerance_index`, `rage_tap_rate`, `default_acceptance_rate`, `pct_kept_default_options_history`, `default_override_frequency`, `tip_rate`, `tip_pct_distribution`, `preselected_addon_accept_rate`, `auto_renew_retention`, `opt_out_friction_response`.
- **Source.** derived. **Grain.** user. **Unlocks.** friction add/remove, checkout, default/opt-in, onboarding, upsell, paywall.

**B8 — Trust / social-proof / scarcity / risk-aversion sensitivity** *(merges PM trust-sensitivity + pricing urgency-responsiveness + pricing trust/risk)*
- **Purpose.** Who is rating/review-driven vs price-driven; who accelerates under scarcity cues vs distrusts them; the trust threshold where urgency *backfires* — the sign-flip moderator for social-proof, scarcity, and guarantee surfaces.
- **Columns.** `reviews_read_rate`, `review_read_depth`, `rating_sensitivity_score`, `scarcity_badge_responsiveness`, `conversion_lift_under_low_stock_history`, `fast_booking_propensity`, `abandons_after_countdown_flag`, `repeat_exposure_fatigue_scarcity`, `skepticism_proxy_review_reads`, `high_rating_merchant_share_ordered`, `new_merchant_trial_rate`, `complaint_rate`, `refund_request_rate`, `first_time_merchant_hesitation`, `guarantee_redeem_history`, `risk_aversion_score`.
- **Source.** derived (impression + conversion logs). **Grain.** user (× merchant). **Unlocks.** trust/social-proof/scarcity, price framing, guarantee surface, ranking.

**B9 — Referral / social-graph propensity**
- **Purpose.** Sign referral tests via demonstrated invite behavior and network connectedness.
- **Columns.** `referrals_sent_lifetime`, `referral_conversion_rate`, `invite_propensity_score`, `social_connectedness_index`.
- **Source.** derived. **Grain.** user. **Unlocks.** referral-program, loyalty/gamification.

**B10 — User proficiency / familiarity / habituation** *(HCI; partly folded into B1 but kept distinct for surface-level muscle memory)*
- **Purpose.** Novices vs power users react oppositely to friction changes; habituation to a specific surface makes a reorder cost regulars (guards the novelty-decay trap).
- **Columns.** `prior_error_rate`, `muscle_memory_path_strength`, `avg_session_friction_baseline`, `feature_adoption_breadth`, `surface_visit_count_90d`.
- **Source.** profile + user×surface. **Grain.** user (+ user×surface). **Unlocks.** nav/IA, layout reorder, friction add/remove, onboarding, default.

### C. Session / interaction telemetry classes

**C1 — Per-surface friction & funnel/flow telemetry** *(merges marketplace session-funnel, PM funnel-step, pricing funnel-friction, HCI per-surface-friction + funnel-flow-step — uses HCI's granular event schema)*
- **Purpose.** The core HCI mechanism signal plus step-resolved completion: measure the effort/error/abandonment delta a UI change induces on each user×surface×step and locate where friction binds, so proximal-funnel direction (and net across steps) is grounded.
- **Columns.** `mistap_rate_30d`, `rage_click_rate_per_session`, `dead_click_rate`, `error_click_rate`, `time_to_first_action_ms_p50`, `median_dwell_ms_on_surface`, `backtrack_rate`, `scroll_depth_to_target_pct`, `tap_target_miss_distance_px`, `step_completion_rate`, `step_abandonment_rate`, `per_field_hesitation_ms`, `validation_error_count_per_step`, `step_count_in_flow`, `form_field_count`, `reverse_step_navigation_rate`, `cart_abandon_step`, `cart_abandon_rate`, `median_time_to_order_sec`, `guest_vs_login_conversion_gap`, `payment_retry_rate`, `save_resume_rate`.
- **Source.** telemetry (+ derived join to transactions). **Grain.** user × surface_id × flow × step × variant × day. **Unlocks.** CTA, layout reorder, nav/IA, checkout/form, onboarding, default, search/filter, friction guardrail, modal, empty/error state.

**C2 — Attention / engagement signals**
- **Purpose.** Where attention lands and for how long, so a reorder/density/media change is scored on capturing attention earlier without overload (Netflix interaction vectors, Airbnb dwell-as-relevance).
- **Columns.** `viewport_impression_count`, `hover_dwell_ms`, `scroll_velocity_px_s`, `scroll_reversal_count`, `scroll_depth_p50`, `items_viewed_before_action`, `above_fold_dwell_share`, `element_view_to_tap_rate`, `truncation_view_without_expand_rate`, `banner_blindness_score`, `carousel_swipe_depth`.
- **Source.** telemetry. **Grain.** user × element_id × surface × session. **Unlocks.** layout reorder, content density/truncation, media/thumbnail, search/filter, CTA.

**C3 — Latency / quality-of-experience / performance** *(merges PM QoE + HCI latency)*
- **Purpose.** Actual and perceived render speed, crashes, and errors — the single best-grounded (near-monotone) direction signal, and a confound for any UI test on slow segments. *(Non-monotone caveat in §4.)*
- **Columns.** `surface_render_ms_p50`, `surface_render_ms_p95`, `time_to_interactive_ms`, `api_response_ms_p95`, `app_latency_p90_ms`, `skeleton_to_content_ms`, `jank_frame_rate`, `cold_start_ms`, `crash_rate`, `payment_error_rate`, `api_timeout_rate`, `connection_class`.
- **Source.** telemetry (RUM). **Grain.** user × surface × session → user×surface×variant. **Unlocks.** latency/perf, empty/error/loading, media/autoplay, CTA, checkout, model swap.

**C4 — Session intent / state**
- **Purpose.** Direction depends on whether the session is high-intent (checkout, latency-sensitive) or low-intent browse; condition predicted direction on the moment.
- **Columns.** `session_intent_score`, `cart_present_flag`, `session_depth_pages`, `is_reorder_session`, `entry_channel` (push|organic|deeplink), `elapsed_session_time_ms`, `time_of_day_bucket`, `screens_per_session`.
- **Source.** derived. **Grain.** user × session. **Unlocks.** modal timing, latency, notification, default, checkout/form.

**C5 — Search / browse intent behavior**
- **Purpose.** Distinguish goal-directed searchers from browsers — the axis that signs ranking, sort-default, and discovery changes.
- **Columns.** `search_to_order_rate`, `browse_vs_search_ratio`, `filters_used_count`, `avg_results_scrolled`, `query_specificity_score`, `query_refinement_count`, `zero_result_abandonment_rate`.
- **Source.** telemetry. **Grain.** user. **Unlocks.** ranking/sort, search/discovery, recommendation.

### D. Context / device classes

**D1 — Device / platform / input-modality / accessibility context** *(merges marketplace, PM, HCI)*
- **Purpose.** Friction and layout outcomes are modality-dependent (touch double-tap vs mouse; small screens truncate; a11y settings change tap targets). Avoids mis-reading platform patterns as frustration (rage-click false-positive).
- **Columns.** `platform` (ios|android|web), `device_tier` (low|high-end), `device_class` (phone|tablet|desktop), `app_version`, `screen_width_px`, `screen_size_bucket`, `input_modality` (touch|mouse|keyboard), `os_platform`, `connection_type`, `dynamic_text_scale`, `reduced_motion_flag`, `rtl_flag`, `locale`, `one_handed_reach_zone_flag`, `is_cold_start`.
- **Source.** telemetry/profile. **Grain.** user × device × session. **Unlocks.** CTA, layout, density, latency, checkout/form, i18n/a11y, net-new launch.

**D2 — Temporal / seasonality / external context** *(merges marketplace external + PM temporal + pricing geo/macro)*
- **Purpose.** Daypart, weather, paydays, holidays, competition, local price level, regulation — condition messaging/promo/pricing outcomes, set outside-option strength, prevent attributing seasonality to treatment, and explain non-replication across markets ("worked in ALDI, fails elsewhere").
- **Columns.** `hour_of_day`, `daypart`, `day_of_week`, `is_holiday`, `weather_severity`, `local_event_flag`, `days_to_payday`, `local_competitor_density`, `competitor_density_zone`, `local_price_level_index`, `regulatory_fee_cap_flag`, `market_maturity_stage`, `seasonality_index`, `macro_demand_trend`, `median_income_zip_external`.
- **Source.** external. **Grain.** market-zone × time/date. **Unlocks.** lifecycle timing, promo, fee/price, surge, ETA.

### E. Entity (supply-side & content) classes

**E1 — Per-item content, quality & price attributes** *(merges marketplace item-quality, PM item, pricing item attrs, HCI surface-content)*
- **Purpose.** The priced/ranked object: per-item conversion, rating, popularity, content completeness, price/margin/dispersion — so ranking/rec/catalog/density/media predictions don't assume uniform content (rich vs sparse listing), and cross-item substitution is computable.
- **Columns.** `item_pcvr`, `item_ctr`, `avg_rating`, `review_count`, `has_photo`, `content_completeness_score`, `median_description_length`, `popularity_rank`, `is_long_tail`, `item_price`, `item_margin_pct`, `price_dispersion_category`, `out_of_stock_rate`, `is_sponsored_flag`, `promo_eligibility_flag`.
- **Source.** transactions/derived/profile. **Grain.** item. **Unlocks.** ranking/sort, recommendation, content density, media, search/filter, supply tooling, fee/price.

**E2 — Per-merchant quality, reliability & economics** *(merges marketplace merchant-quality + PM merchant-quality + merchant-economics)*
- **Purpose.** The other-side entity: operational reliability, fulfillment, selection, ratings AND commission/ad/tenure economics — grounds ranking, trust, ETA, supply-tooling, commission tests and the merchant-side OEC of any consumer change.
- **Columns.** `merchant_pcvr`, `merchant_rating`, `rating_p50`, `review_count`, `fulfillment_reliability`, `reliability_score`, `avg_prep_time`, `prep_time_p50`, `cancel_rate`, `menu_breadth`, `menu_depth`, `photo_coverage`, `item_in_stock_rate`, `is_new_merchant`, `commission_rate`, `ad_spend_l30d`, `merchant_conversion_rate`, `avg_basket_at_merchant`, `merchant_price_index_vs_peers`, `tenure_on_platform_days`, `catalog_freshness_days`.
- **Source.** transactions. **Grain.** merchant. **Unlocks.** supply tooling, ranking, ETA/availability, dispatch, trust, commission/supply-incentive, fee/price.

**E3 — Treatment-surface position & composition metadata** *(merges marketplace surface-position + HCI surface-composition)*
- **Purpose.** Where in the journey the change lives AND what each variant actually renders, so the engine can featurize the *change itself* (delta in element count, text length, target size, funnel depth) and scale any predicted effect by surface leverage — generalizing across surfaces instead of memorizing one screen.
- **Columns.** `funnel_depth_of_surface`, `baseline_traffic_share`, `baseline_drop_rate_at_surface`, `above_fold_flag`, `exposure_rate`, `competes_for_attention_with`, `interactive_element_count`, `primary_cta_size_px`, `primary_cta_contrast_ratio`, `text_char_length`, `is_truncated_flag`, `above_fold_module_count`, `tap_target_min_size_px`, `media_present_flag`, `default_preselected_flag`, `step_count`.
- **Source.** derived (layout/DOM/design metadata). **Grain.** surface_id × variant. **Unlocks.** CTA, layout, copy, density, default, nav, media, ranking.

### F. Marketplace-equilibrium classes

**F1 — Market supply/demand balance (market-state)** *(merges marketplace liquidity + PM geo-balance + pricing supply/demand)*
- **Purpose.** Geo×time conditioning state that *mediates* two-sided experiments; the unit switchback/cluster designs randomize on. **Conditions but does not identify** the two-sided sign from per-user data (see §4).
- **Columns.** `supply_demand_ratio`, `courier_supply_demand_ratio_zone_hour`, `active_supply_count`, `open_orders`, `order_backlog_zone`, `avg_eta_min`, `surge_active`, `surge_multiplier_active`, `undersupplied_flag`, `busyness_index`, `merchant_capacity_utilization`, `fulfillment_rate_zone_trailing_1h`, `market_maturity`, `active_selection_count`.
- **Source.** telemetry/derived. **Grain.** market-zone × time-bucket (hour). **Unlocks.** surge/dynamic pricing, supply-incentive, dispatch/batching, promo, ETA.

**F2 — Cross-side / network spillover & cannibalization**
- **Purpose.** Cannibalization/interference signals: how a treatment on one side/segment shifts the others (consumer fee cut raises courier load; promoting one merchant demotes substitutes). Grain mismatch with per-user randomization is the core marketplace bias source — a *partial proxy only*.
- **Columns.** `substitute_share_overlap`, `cannibalization_index`, `cross_side_load_delta`, `cluster_interference_flag`, `market_share_of_treated_supply`.
- **Source.** derived. **Grain.** per-market / per-cluster. **Unlocks.** dispatch, ranking (volume), surge/fee, supply tooling.

**F3 — Network-structure / cluster-assignment / interference-exposure** *(critic add — the missing asset for switchback/cluster identification)*
- **Purpose.** F1/F2 are aggregates; identifying interference-dominated signs needs graph position, neighbor-treatment exposure, and cluster ids. Without this, the two-sided experiment types are "unlocked" in name only.
- **Columns.** `cluster_id`, `graph_degree`, `neighbor_treated_share`, `interference_exposure_score`, `switchback_window_id`, `treated_neighbor_count`.
- **Source.** derived. **Grain.** user × cluster × time-window. **Unlocks.** surge/dynamic pricing, dispatch/batching, supply-incentive (as a *design enabler*, not a tabular predictor).

### G. Acquisition & semantic classes *(critic adds)*

**G1 — Anonymous / pre-login visitor & device-graph** *(critic add — closes the top-of-funnel gap)*
- **Purpose.** First-touch channel, device fingerprint/graph, logged-out session behavior, attribution — required to ground any acquisition/landing/app-store/logged-out experiment. A `user_id`-keyed store structurally cannot hold the cold visitor.
- **Columns.** `visitor_id`, `first_touch_channel`, `attribution_source`, `device_fingerprint_hash`, `device_graph_cluster`, `loggedout_session_count`, `landing_page_id`, `referrer_domain`, `utm_campaign`, `install_attribution_source`.
- **Source.** telemetry. **Grain.** visitor_id (pre-login) / device. **Unlocks.** acquisition/marketing-creative, landing/SEO, app-store listing, logged-out web.

**G2 — Creative / copy / image semantic-embedding** *(critic add — the concrete bridge instead of "hand it to an LLM")*
- **Purpose.** Text/image embeddings + LLM-judge score per variant, the bridge feature that lets the empirical store separate *within-type creative quality* rather than abstaining entirely. Deferrable, but its omission is a schema gap.
- **Columns.** `copy_text_embedding_768d`, `image_embedding_512d`, `llm_judge_clarity_score`, `llm_judge_persuasion_score`, `readability_grade`, `sentiment_polarity`, `headline_specificity_score`, `visual_salience_score`.
- **Source.** derived (LLM/embedding layer). **Grain.** surface_id × variant. **Unlocks.** copy/microcopy (creative-quality slice), media/thumbnail, social-proof copy — *low-confidence, abstain-leaning*.

### H. Guard / validity classes (gates, not predictors)

**H1 — Negative-control / confound guard**
- **Purpose.** Held-out outcomes that should NOT move + pre-treatment balance. A gate, not a predictor: if the observational sign is driven by unobserved confounding, the NC fires and the engine **abstains** rather than emitting a confident wrong sign. *Buys abstention, not correctness — and only if the NC is strongly coupled to the latent confounder (§4).*
- **Columns.** `neg_control_outcome_l1..k`, `pre_treatment_metric_balance`, `placebo_segment_effect`, `confound_proxy_drift`, `guard_floor_violation_flag`, `neg_control_ratio` (floor=0.05, ratio=1.5 — ported from `causal_estimator.py`).
- **Source.** derived. **Grain.** per-experiment (× segment). **Unlocks.** gates fee/price, ranking, recommendation, net-new, any observational read.

**H2 — Assignment-validity & instrumentation guard** *(critic add — distinct from NC)*
- **Purpose.** The most common reasons a measured sign is an *artifact*: sample-ratio mismatch, broken/diluted exposure logging, trigger dilution, peeking. Distinct gates from neg-controls.
- **Columns.** `srm_pvalue`, `exposure_log_completeness`, `trigger_dilution_rate`, `peeking_violation_flag`, `assignment_imbalance_flag`, `variance_inflation_estimate`.
- **Source.** derived. **Grain.** per-experiment. **Unlocks.** gates every type before a sign is trusted.

**H3 — Consent / instrumentation-coverage / data-quality** *(critic add)*
- **Purpose.** Consent-state and per-user logging coverage gate whether telemetry-derived classes even *exist* for a user; without them the engine treats missing-because-unconsented as a real-zero and mis-signs the affected segment.
- **Columns.** `att_consent_flag`, `analytics_consent_flag`, `telemetry_coverage_score`, `logging_gap_flag`, `feature_missingness_rate`.
- **Source.** derived. **Grain.** user. **Unlocks.** gates all telemetry-derived classes (C*, B6, attention).

### I. Longitudinal & cross-experiment classes *(critic adds — mitigate the universally-named blind spots)*

**I1 — Longitudinal / time-since-exposure response curve (novelty-decay instrumentation)**
- **Purpose.** All four lenses name novelty decay but none proposes the mitigation: per-user exposure age and response-over-time slope so a day-1 vs day-30 sign flip (a reorder that looks worse on day 1 wins at day 30) is recoverable instead of a static-snapshot artifact.
- **Columns.** `exposure_age_days`, `response_slope_d1_d30`, `habituation_curve_halflife`, `novelty_lift_decay_rate`, `day1_vs_day30_metric_delta`, `cumulative_exposure_count`.
- **Source.** derived. **Grain.** user × treatment × time-since-exposure. **Unlocks.** UI/copy/feature types with novelty risk; notification; gates short-window reads.

**I2 — Long-horizon surrogate / proxy-metric**
- **Purpose.** The standard mitigation for the LTV/retention blind spot: short-term proxies calibrated against measured long-term outcomes (Netflix proxy-metric practice), so "short-run conversion up, LTV down" is at least partially proxied rather than undetectable.
- **Columns.** `surrogate_ltv_index`, `proxy_retention_d30_pred`, `early_signal_to_ltv_calibration`, `deal_seeking_training_proxy`, `return_regret_proxy_score`.
- **Source.** derived. **Grain.** user × treatment. **Unlocks.** distal-sign check on fee/promo, paywall, friction-removal, notification.

**I3 — Cross-experiment concurrency / interaction**
- **Purpose.** With 1000s of concurrent tests, the marginal direction of one depends on co-running arms; without this every prior-treatment-response feature (A1) is confounded by un-modeled simultaneous treatments.
- **Columns.** `concurrent_arm_ids`, `co_running_treatment_count`, `interaction_collision_flag`, `shared_surface_experiment_overlap`.
- **Source.** experiment-history. **Grain.** user × time-window. **Unlocks.** gates/conditions A1 priors for all types.

| Experiment type | Core required classes | Moderators (M) | Guards (G) |

| CTA copy/affordance/placement | C1, E3, C2 | D1, B10, G2 | H1, I1 |

| Copy / microcopy | E3, **G2** | C1, B8 | I1 (abstain-leaning) |
| Form / checkout step & field count | C1, B7 | B1, D1 | H2 (proximal→distal) |
| Checkout / cart friction reduction | C1, B7 | B1, C4 | **I2** (returns/regret), H1 |

## 4. The Answerable-vs-Abstain Boundary

**Honest union coverage for DIRECTION prediction: ~35–45% of a real consumer-marketplace roadmap at usefully-better-than-chance, and only ~10–20% on the decision-relevant counter-intuitive subset.** For a *new* org (empty A1), real coverage drops to ~25–30%. Report the counter-intuitive number as the product ceiling; design for **abstention + external-validity auditing**, not blanket prediction.

**Derivation.**
- **Base-rate cap.** ~1/3 of experiments are statistically FLAT and another large share underpowered (Microsoft: 1/3 positive / 1/3 flat / 1/3 negative; Google/Bing: 10–20% positive). For the flat/tiny third, "direction" is ill-posed — no predictor can win there.
- **Per-family groundability of the non-null remainder.** UI/copy/flow/onboarding (~40–55% of volume) → ~50–60% (only ~half is friction-expressible vs aesthetic/relevance ties; a slice has proximal→distal inversion). Pricing/promo (~15–20%) → ~50% (only where the lever historically varied and isn't interference-dominated). Ranking/recs (~10–15%) → ~50% (relevance ties + offline→online gap). Notification/lifecycle (~5–10%) → ~50% (proximal-yes/distal-no). Supply-side/equilibrium/dispatch (~5–10%) → **~15%** (needs switchback, not a feature store). Net-new/brand (~5%) → **~0%**.
- **Entirely-missing slices** (acquisition/marketing, support/service, returns/refunds, privacy/compliance, merchant-as-user) ≈ 10–15% of roadmap at **0–partial** coverage without G1 and a supplier entity.

**Abstain-only types and why:**
1. **Net-new surfaces with no behavioral analog** — A1, B5, friction priors are all empty; the surface never existed. Hard floor.
2. **Pure aesthetic / brand / taste** (button color, hero image, palette, rename) — equally-usable variants give identical friction telemetry; G2 embeddings are weak and novelty-confounded. Booking's button-color win was *found by testing, not predicted.*
3. **Two-sided / surge / dispatch / supply-incentive** — market-state (F1) *conditions* but cannot *identify* the sign from per-user randomized data; interference requires switchback/cluster design (F3 enables the design, not a tabular read). Listing these as "unlocked" by F1 alone is the council's internal contradiction.
4. **Long-horizon / LTV / retention vs short-run conversion** — a fee cut or promo lifts orders today and erodes margin/trains deal-seeking tomorrow; only *partially* proxied by I2 surrogates.
5. **Novelty / primacy decay** — without I1 trajectory features the store is a static snapshot and the durable sign is unrecoverable.
6. **Proximal→distal sign inversion** (one-click checkout ↑conversion ↑returns; extra push ↑opens ↑churn; removed confirmation ↓effort ↑refund/chargeback) — friction telemetry counts the *wrong-signed proxy*; needs I2 + the economics lens to own the distal sign.
7. **Counter-intuitive cross-segment trade-down** — the engine "tracks intuition not truth" (internal blind tests: weak on counter-intuitive cases; e.g. a price-transparency feature that reads as a trade-down accelerator among high-value users — predicted positive, measured negative). Requires explicit heterogeneity modeling, not average-effect features.
8. **Per-user elasticity / per-user CATE** are *model-imputed, not measured* — price is policy-set (endogenous, scarce within-user variation); per-user treatment effect is fundamentally unobservable. Schematized as columns (B3, A1 `historical_HTE_decile`) but flagged: these overstate identifiability and must carry uncertainty.
9. **A1 itself is mostly empty or noisy** — company cold-start, an unsolved similar-treatment retrieval problem, drifting surface taxonomies / redefined metrics (Minerva), and base rates where most "prior signs" are null/underpowered.
10. **Latency "faster=better" is high- but not universal-confidence** — documented non-monotone cases (too-fast reads as untrustworthy; faster surfacing raises choice overload).
11. **NC guard buys abstention, not correctness** — only if the negative control is strongly coupled to the latent confounder (the team's own work: needs LLM-picked strongly-coupled NC; flagged 0/3 errors before the guard existed).
12. **External validity / generalization of a win** — an effect estimated where the lever varied may invert elsewhere; the store flags heterogeneity + neg-controls but *auditing transfer is its own product wedge*, not a direct schema output.

This matches the internal finding: the causal/uplift route works only for the **feature-expressible slice — a router, not an LLM replacement.**

---

## 5. Build-Cost / Priority Ordering (minimal high-leverage subset)

Ingest for maximum *experiment-type coverage per unit of data-engineering effort*. Each wave is independently useful and gates the next.

**Wave 0 — Guards first (cheap, prevent confident-wrong).** H1 (negative-control), H2 (SRM/exposure-validity), H3 (consent/coverage). These are per-experiment derivations over data you already log; they convert the whole system from "predicts" to "predicts or abstains." Build before any prediction ships.

**Wave 1 — The reusable spine (covers the most types per table).**
1. **B1 Lifecycle+RFM+habit** — derivable from transactions alone; the most-reused moderator, touches nearly every type.
2. **A2 CUPED pre-period covariates** — same transactional source; unlocks *detectability* for every powered test.
3. **C1 Friction & funnel telemetry** — the single class that grounds the largest roadmap slice (all UI/flow/checkout/onboarding). Highest event-engineering cost but highest volume payoff.
4. **A1 Experiment-history prior store (start at surface×family×metric grain)** — the dominant anchor; begin logging *every* shipped experiment's change-type + measured sign now, even if sparse, because it only compounds.

**Wave 2 — Pricing & ranking unlock (high decision value).**
5. **B3 Elasticity & deal-proneness** + **B4 reference-price** — unlock the pricing/promo family (the highest-stakes, most-confounded slice); requires historical fee/price variation, so co-ingest the impression/offer logs.
6. **E1 item + E2 merchant** entity tables — unlock ranking/rec/trust/supply; reuse existing catalog/ops data.
7. **B5 preference/substitution** — unlock personalization/recs and cross-elasticity.

**Wave 3 — Context & messaging.**
8. **D1 device/context** + **C3 latency** — cheap RUM/telemetry; unlock latency/perf and segment-correct UI.
9. **B6 channel responsiveness & fatigue** — unlock the notification/lifecycle family.
10. **D2 temporal/external** — third-party feeds; condition pricing/promo and prevent seasonality artifacts.

**Wave 4 — The blind-spot mitigations (build once the spine produces wins worth auditing).**
11. **I1 longitudinal / novelty-decay** + **I2 long-horizon surrogate** — convert short-window signs into durable ones; required before trusting any UI/promo/notification distal claim.
12. **F1 market-state** + **F3 cluster/interference** — only worth it alongside switchback/cluster *design*; without the design they don't identify two-sided signs.
13. **G1 anonymous-visitor** (separate entity, opens acquisition) and **G2 creative embeddings** (opens the within-type creative slice) — highest marginal cost, lowest confidence; build last.

**Rule of thumb.** Waves 0–1 alone reach the bulk of the ~35–45% groundable roadmap (UI/flow + the reusable moderators + guards). Waves 2–3 add the high-value pricing/ranking/messaging families. Wave 4 buys honesty (abstention quality, durable signs, two-sided design) rather than new coverage.

---

## 6. Tie-In: Per-Pack Capability Score

A persona/feature **pack** is scored against this schema by, for each of the 24 feature classes, computing three sub-scores: **presence** (does the pack carry the class's load-bearing columns — e.g. B3 needs observed fee variation, A1 needs prior-experiment rows), **variance** (does the lever/moderator actually *vary* in the pack — a fee column that never moves cannot identify elasticity; this is the §4 cold-start/endogeneity guard made operational), and **support** (sample size / grain coverage / consent-coverage from H3, so a thinly-populated class doesn't masquerade as answerable). The class scores roll up — weighted by each class's roadmap-coverage contribution from §3/§5 — into a single **capability score N**, and the engine reports it as: *"This pack scores **N/100**. With present-and-varying classes {B1, C1, A2, E1…} it can ground **direction** for {checkout-friction, layout, latency, ranking…} experiment types; it must **abstain** on {surge, net-new, aesthetic, long-horizon} for lack of {F3, I2, G2} or for structural reasons; to extend coverage, ingest {B3 with historical fee variation, A1 prior rows, B6 channel logs} next."* The same presence/variance/support gate that produces N is what fires the H1/H2 abstention at prediction time — so the capability score and the run-time answer/abstain decision are the *same measurement* applied at pack-build vs. experiment-time, keeping the store and the engine that consumes it in lockstep.
